context.label: Weeks, harvest, and the fiftieth day

observations.body: Seven weeks are counted from the beginning of harvest; a freewill gift reflects blessing, and household, servants, Levite, foreigner, orphan, and widow rejoice together while slavery is remembered.
observations.label: Weeks begins with the sickle and widens into shared joy

observations.body: The passage presents Counting, giving, and rejoicing as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Counting, giving, and rejoicing

observations.body: The passage places Remembering slavery beside Counting, giving, and rejoicing.
observations.label: Remembering slavery

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 16:9–12 as one movement in Pentecost, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states seven weeks are counted from the beginning of harvest; a freewill gift reflects blessing, and household, servants, Levite, foreigner, orphan, and widow rejoice together while slavery is remembered. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Pentecost.
payload.title: Weeks begins with the sickle and widens into shared joy
